name: PLE page reclaim and prefetch admission
exact: Stored rows, IQ4_NL decoding, BF16 conversion and staging offsets are unchanged. CPU byte equality covers 200,000-position plain and MTP prefill/decode streams with the source mapping protected against reads. Native GPU token/logit/state and complete-workload qualification remain required for O_DIRECT rolling; GSQ page-drop behavior is not qualified.
gain: Capacity admission for T8192 at 128K/262K; no isolated speed attribution
preconditions: Linux, nonempty plain CLI prompt, tiled known prefill, registered file mapping, one valid IQ4_NL/BF16 PLE table with unregistered interior pages, verified setup drop and supported O_DIRECT reads. No model copy/promotion, graph, cohort, HTTP/serving, session load/live/follow-up, fixed MTP session or planned PLE IO. Plain prefix-cache restore/import and follow-up prompt routes retain the public prompt-wide planner; numerical snapshots never retain rolling source leases. Eager MTP retains required assets, explicit turn leases and phase-owned critical-first asynchronous prompt lookahead/c1 staging, with original offsets and turn/epoch/offset-validated pinned views. Calibration and decode drain the prompt pipeline, including pending staging tasks. Adaptive R2/R4/R8 row sets and min-p are covered by complete physical-window source leases including padding within the fixed decode quota; rejection/replay reuses or re-fetches owned bytes. Depth/survival controllers, copy-wide rows, golden dump, metadata-only, recording and sampled timing schedules remain excluded with specific inactive reasons. Cost-adaptive min-p schedules remain unchanged and require native token/logit/state qualification. Rolling uses owned aligned buffers with a shared 3 GiB default STRIX_PLE_ROLLING_CAP_BYTES cap plus fixed 256 MiB decode LRU and margin; allocation and inspection share admission arithmetic and separately charge metadata. Raw Linux io_uring uses 512 outstanding reads, a dedicated submission/completion thread and at most 128 KiB coalesced runs, without liburing. Unsupported setup/opcode detection (ENOSYS/EPERM/EINVAL) selects the checked O_DIRECT 32-thread pread fallback and reports its errno/backend. The setup helper completes each next-block read wave before later lookahead; critical demand promotes shared queued runs and pauses lookahead dispatch until critical completion. Small caps split ordered waves. STATS includes per-block critical bytes, completion-span application IOPS/MB/s and completed lookahead bytes. Plain c1/lookahead retains its original chunks and offsets, splitting/throttling under cap pressure. No rolling hot-path madvise/fadvise/mincore; table-wide residency is observed only at setup and drained request ends. Automatic setup failures tear down provisional owners, remove all credit and require fresh zero-credit resident admission before warming, retaining the MTP policy. Required mode refuses. Runtime read failures poison the source and exit nonzero; resident restart requires a fresh invocation.
off_switch: STRIX_PLE_RECLAIMABLE=0 disables reclaim. STRIX_PLE_ROLLING=0 or STRIX_CTX_EXACT_MEMORY=0 restores the previous plain prompt-wide mmap path and MTP warm path, ignoring rolling tuning.

name: Memory-admitted prefill chunk rows
default: 8192 for two-rank decode prompt prefill when both ranks fit, otherwise 4096; reference prefill and no-handshake harnesses keep 4096
exact: Measured 8192-row chunks produce the same logits and tokens as 4096 on the exact prefill route; chunk size preserves its arithmetic.
gain: Chunked-prefill route at 8192 rows: 8K TTFT -4 %; 32K 116.3 -> 109.9 s (-5.5 %); about 7.3 GiB additional GPU memory per node; --pf-ttft requires explicit --max-rows 8192 to measure this
preconditions: Omitted --max-rows outside baseline. The 8192 default applies to prompt prefill in two-rank decode runs, including production decode with MTP self-speculation and plain chunked prefill inside --decode runs, when memory allows. Reference prefill (--prefill ref, automatic prefill under r1b-all or --idcheck with decode) keeps 4096 with source auto-4096-ref, without auto admission or a row-count agreement exchange. The calibrated load admission terms (physical plan, forward reserve, pinned staging, whole-tensor reads and bounce), RAM headroom after free CMA and CMA file pages, GTT headroom and margins, prefill path/workspace/install, communication growth and device-free guard must admit 8192. Retain the largest RAM margin of 8 GiB, load and prefill; otherwise choose 4096. Normal two-rank Comm decode reuses the existing eligibility exchange and OR vote: spare config bit for auto, negative row value for rank minimum; mixed auto/fixed refuses on both ranks. Fixed payload bytes, message count and tags are unchanged. After communication growth, a fresh admission check uses one auto-only minimum vote and shrinks both pools on a 4096 fallback. No common configuration exchange exists for prefill-only, reference gates or batch-only runs: Comm auto uses 4096 with source auto-4096-no-handshake, resolved independently from local flags before inspection or engine construction without a control exchange; --pf-ttft and gate harnesses keep 4096 unless --max-rows 8192 is explicit; fixed max_rows equality cannot be checked there without changing the protocol. External Xfer auto uses 4096 without any agreement exchange. Auto communication buffers start at 4096 and grow only after agreement on 8192, so fallback has off-switch capacity. Existing allocation guards protect against changing memory pressure. Inspection is host-independent; stderr reports headroom and final source.
off_switch: STRIX_GLM_MAX_ROWS_AUTO=0 restores fixed 4096; --max-rows N keeps N; --baseline keeps 1024 unless explicitly overridden
